page: Microsoft Azure E96-24s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine utilizing a constrained-core configuration. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating up to 4.2 GHz. The instance provisions 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It incorporates 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache pool. Hardware instruction flags include AVX-512 extensions and Intel AMX matrix acceleration engines for vector and deep learning computations.

The primary characteristic of this instance is its high memory density, pairing 768.0 GB of RAM with 24 vCPUs, yielding 32.0 GB of memory per vCPU. The server carries no local storage, requiring attached network volumes via its Premium Storage capable storage bus, and includes no discrete graphics processing units. In memory benchmarks, it recorded 187.67 GB/sec in uncached read operations and a strong 116.85 GB/sec in uncached 256 MB write throughput.

Benchmark data reflects strong single-thread efficiency alongside solid memory execution. The instance posted a Geekbench single-core score of 2142.0, placing in the top quartile, while its multi-core result reached 15298.0 in the middle tier. In workload-specific testing, it yielded strong scores in image and text processing tasks, as well as 294.92 tokens per second in small model LLM text generation. Redis operations reached 35.07 million SET commands per second.

By restricting active compute to 24 vCPUs on a chassis capable of supporting 96 vCPU memory tiers, this instance provides cost efficiency for software environments licensed per core that demand massive working sets. The profile is directly applicable to in-memory caching systems, transactional databases, and large analytics engines requiring high memory-to-core ratios without excess compute licensing overhead.

The system provides 768.0 GB of RAM, establishing a ratio of 32.0 GB per vCPU, supported by 260 MB of L3 cache. It contains no local storage and no GPUs, relying on remote block volumes. Benchmark metrics highlight strong single-core CPU performance alongside high uncached write memory bandwidth of 116.85 GB/sec and strong image and text processing scores. Multithreaded execution, compression, and general integer compute fall squarely into average tiers. This constrained-vCPU hardware allocation provides qualitative cost advantages for memory-bound workloads facing core-based software licensing costs, such as large in-memory databases, enterprise caching layers, and high-footprint data processing pipelines.
